outputs.name: connections.json

a link named 'workshop' in the session's boot plan, admitted by that Workshop
zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in the session host (Workshop's shapes, declared there)
tools.recovery: 'unlinked' means the link has no far session (the Workshop is not running or refused this host: see loom-session status). A dispatch refusal from Workshop means its guests file does not let this host 'inspect'.

tools.name: inspect-capture
tools.summary: Inspect a running Workshop, take its picture, press a key chord through an input session, and take the picture again.
tools.description: The journey, in order, each step checked against its owner's answer: the link's own session; this session's row in the guest door's inventory; an input session from zengine.input; a picture of what Workshop presents, fetched chunk by chunk and checked whole; optionally a picture ARMED for the next painted frame, so a capture waits at Workshop's Skin; optionally a hold at a release gate; an optional click that points at a pane, and the chord, injected together with settlement, so the answer comes back only once Workshop has dispatched everything the injection set in motion; the armed picture, if any; the picture after the chord; the session closed. Every failure after the session opened closes it first, and says both.

inputs.name: link
inputs.help: the external host's link to the Workshop

inputs.name: chord
inputs.help: the key chord to press, e.g. ctrl+p, down, escape, ctrl+shift+f -- pass empty (with a non-empty `click`) for a click-only batch, no chord following it: often the right choice for a click that may open a menu, since ANY key afterward -- even one this pane binds to nothing -- is itself a newer gesture that can make Workshop refuse the very menu the click opened as 'late' (workshop/weave_external.cpp); `clear`, `text` and `repeat` all need a chord and are refused with an empty one

inputs.name: text
inputs.help: text to type after the chord (plain order) or after clearing (clear order); needs a non-empty `chord`

inputs.name: arm
inputs.help: ask for the picture of the next painted frame BEFORE the batch, so a real capture is pending at Workshop's Skin until its repaint answers it

inputs.name: click
inputs.help: point at a pane before the chord: 'x,y' in the SDL skin's pixels, or 'x,yc' in the terminal skins' cells -- empty presses the chord with no click first. With `chord` also empty, the click is the whole batch

inputs.name: button
inputs.help: which button `click` presses: left, middle or right -- right is a pane's own second route to its context menu where the menu declares no key (a line open for typing keeps every letter, so the menu cannot also own one); ignored when click is empty

inputs.name: clear
inputs.help: a typed field's own order: Ctrl+A (select all -- component/text_box.hpp) to take the whole field regardless of its length or the caret's position, then Backspace to erase that selection (whether or not `text` follows -- an empty `text` types nothing, so the erase cannot be left to typing alone), then `text` if given, then the chord that commits it (Return) -- rather than this tool's plain order, the chord first and text typed into what it opened. Needs a non-empty `chord` to commit with

inputs.name: repeat
inputs.help: press and release `chord` this many times in the one injected batch -- a hand tapping the same key again (row down x6 to walk a list), never the platform's own key-repeat (which holds and never releases between taps); refused before it asks Workshop anything if the batch this makes would pass InjectInput's 64-moment ceiling. Ignored when `clear` is set (clearing's own order presses the chord once, to commit)

inputs.name: hold
inputs.help: hold before the chord until <run>/release/<hold> exists; empty: never

inputs.name: await_repaint
inputs.help: with arm: wait for Workshop to paint by itself before pressing the chord -- for a Workshop that changes on its own

inputs.name: await_seconds
inputs.help: how long await_repaint waits: this tool's own decision to stop waiting, never a verdict about Workshop

inputs.name: changed
inputs.help: require the picture after the chord to differ from the one before it

inputs.name: bug_after
inputs.help: raise an error on purpose after this step (inspect, open, inject) -- a tool bug, for seeing failure and cleanup

outputs.name: connections.json
outputs.help: the guest door's inventory, as answered

outputs.name: before.<bmp|cells.txt>
outputs.help: what Workshop presented once the input session was open

outputs.name: armed.<bmp|cells.txt>
outputs.help: with arm: the picture that waited at the Skin for the next painted frame

outputs.name: after.<bmp|cells.txt>
outputs.help: what it presented after everything the chord set in motion was dispatched

zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in the session host
the input session free: Workshop admits one holder at a time, and every run on one link is the same holder to it
tools.recovery: An input session refused as 'busy' means another holder has it -- on the same link, that is another run of this session, because Workshop sees every run on one link as one participant: wait for it, or use a second link. 'lost' means the link went down after a request was submitted: its outcome is UNKNOWN and nothing is resent; Workshop's guest door closes a lost guest's input session itself. A picture refused 'one waits at a time' means another capture is armed at the Skin.

tools.name: verify-recipe
tools.summary: Read one recipe back from the project's own build-recipes.json, on the local filesystem, and check named fields against it.
tools.description: Opens `<project>/<recipes_file>` (default `build-recipes.json`) directly with this host's own filesystem access -- never through zengine.input, zengine.skin or any other guest door, and never an ask Workshop answers -- finds the one row named `recipe`, and checks every field a caller named an expectation for. Refuses (naming why) a missing file, a file that does not read as `zengine-build-recipes`, zero or several rows under the same name, a `cmake_target` asked about that is not exactly one row, or a run that named no field at all. This is a LOCAL OBSERVATION of what is on disk now, not a claim about who wrote it or when -- pair it with `inspect-capture`'s own settlement, and a file timestamp or a before/after comparison, for a claim about causation.

inputs.name: artifact_blank
inputs.help: check `artifact` is exactly empty, when the expected value itself is the empty string

inputs.name: artifact_dir

inputs.name: artifact_dir_blank
inputs.help: check `artifact_dir` is exactly empty

inputs.name: cmake_target
inputs.help: expected `cmake_target[0].target`; checked only if given, or if `cmake_target_blank` is set

inputs.name: cmake_target_blank
inputs.help: check `cmake_target[0].target` is exactly empty

inputs.name: cmake_config
inputs.help: expected `cmake_target[0].config`; checked only if given, or if `cmake_config_blank` is set -- this recipe field is what the corrections arc's fifth field writes

inputs.name: cmake_config_blank
inputs.help: check `cmake_target[0].config` is exactly empty (a single-config tree's own row)

inputs.name: cmake_build_dir
inputs.help: expected `cmake_target[0].build_dir`; checked only if given, or if `cmake_build_dir_blank` is set

inputs.name: cmake_build_dir_blank
inputs.help: check `cmake_target[0].build_dir` is exactly empty

inputs.name: cmake_entry
inputs.help: expected `cmake_target[0].entry`; checked only if given, or if `cmake_entry_blank` is set

inputs.name: cmake_entry_blank
inputs.help: check `cmake_target[0].entry` is exactly empty

outputs.name: recipe.json
outputs.help: the one matched row, exactly as read from the file

requires: a `build-recipes.json` (or the named `recipes_file`) already written inside `project`, readable by this host's own filesystem access
tools.example: loom-session run <dir> workshop/verify-recipe --name check --input project=<dir> --input recipe=multi --input cmake_config=Release
tools.recovery: A refusal names the exact mismatch or the exact structural problem (missing file, wrong format, zero or several rows under one name) -- there is no other outcome to recover from; fix the expectation or the recipe and run again.

tools.description: restore replaces the connected Workshop's Inventory with a packaged toolbox in one request and rediscovers its four entries by name: the flat inspection-workbench file (the default, a version 1 file read at the root) or, with variant=organized, inspection-workbench-organized. story runs the maker story through visible controls: name three Info views, finish the incomplete capture preset from the sample field to field, save/close/reopen it, submit it through Compose, watch a linked note while another view changes it, keep a dirty draft through a stale save, and sample the sample's source again. folders runs the organized story, reading the stored organization by name every time: drill down to the sample and keep it in the Sample view, climb by a crumb to the preset's folder and link it in the Preset view, fill its target from the sample and save, then rename the command's folder and move Drafts while the command stays in its row with its hotkey OFF; save= writes the result for a fresh instance to restore. retrieve brings the sample into the Sample view the way a maker finds it in either toolbox, for comparison. menus, in the organized toolbox, types in Info while choosing folder menu rows that wait for a key -- Move then Escape, Remove empty folder (on a Scratch folder it made) then Delete -- and files the note onto [Up] and back, so the organization ends as it began. prepare and organize rebuild the packaged files (maintainers). Use an isolated demo Workshop (demo.py --setup workbench or folders); restore replaces its collection.

restore before story, folders or retrieve; organize after restoring the flat file in a Workshop without folders
tools.example: loom-session run <session-dir> workshop/workbench --name restore --input phase=restore --input variant=organized --wait 60
tools.recovery: Restore again to return to a packaged baseline; it replaces this Workshop's collection. A refused step names its view and leaves drafts in place; read workbench.json and the named pictures. Sampling never runs stored commands, and organizing or browsing never runs them either; a pending sample may stay pending, and Stop (Escape) or closing its view twice abandons it with nothing claimed. Run each phase with --wait so the next begins after it ends.

tools.name: editor-materials-demo
tools.summary: Carry text, a Terminal command and a file place between the Editor and named Inventory folders, keep them in a toolbox, and bring them back in another Workshop.
tools.description: A state-reactive story through the standard Editor, Inventory, its folders and the Terminal, read from the owners' current answers. prepare: a timed linear sweep selects text, a Bezier drag from the highlight files a copy into Snippets, right-click Extract files another, ctrl+l files this file's place into Places, a real Terminal SurfaceText capture filed into Commands drops back as generated C++ (then undone) and as its Terminal line, the place is refused over unsaved work and then reopens its line, and the toolbox is saved. keyboard: ctrl+e and ctrl+l pick up, a click places, and Enter picks a stored copy up for a click in the Editor. retrieve: in a fresh Workshop, the toolbox is restored and the place and the snippet come back. neovim (start the demo with --neovim <program>): a Visual selection dragged out along a Bezier, ctrl+r for a linewise one, a stored copy dropped in and undone, and a captured command whose Terminal line is chosen while Neovim waits for input -- held and said so, put in when Escape ends the wait, then undone. Writes beat.cpp and notes.txt into `folder` when missing; creates Snippets, Commands and Places when missing; keeps every entry it makes. Nothing dropped is sent, saved or built.

tools.name: act
tools.summary: Act on Workshop through short named steps -- chords, text, presses on painted rows and controls -- and check each by the rows a pane paints, without pictures.
tools.description: Runs a JSON list of steps in order through one input session. Gestures: press (a chord, optionally repeated), type (one TextEntered moment; newlines included), select (walk a list's cursor -- the row painted with a leading > -- with Down and Up until it names exactly the given row, then stop; bounded, and a name no row or several rows carry fails with the rows painted), into and click (press where Workshop paints a row holding some text, found by PaneView and located by PanePoint), control (a visible [label]). Observations: expect and absent (wait until a pane paints, or stops painting, a row holding some text), rows (keep a pane's rows), picture (keep a capture), wait (a pause). A pane's rows are its presentation: expect proves Workshop painted something, not that the owner painted about finished; pair it with the owner's own evidence. The first step that cannot be done ends the run naming its index and verb; nothing after it is sent.

inputs.name: link
inputs.help: the admitted Workshop link

inputs.name: steps
inputs.help: a JSON list; each item names exactly one verb. {"press": "ctrl+p", "repeat": 2}, {"type": "text"}, {"open": "Files"} (the pane the Pane Manager lists by that name), {"select": [provider, pane, name]} (the list row named exactly that, reached by Down/Up, whatever sorts before it), {"into": [provider, pane, text?]}, {"click": [provider, pane, text], "button": "right"}, {"at": [provider, pane, row, column]} (one painted cell, counted from 0), {"control": [provider, pane, label]}, {"expect": [provider, pane, text], "seconds": 10}, {"absent": [...]}, {"rows": [provider, pane], "as": name}, {"picture": name, "png": true, "crop": [x0, y0, x1, y1], "save": absolute .png path}, {"wait": seconds}

inputs.name: pace_ms
inputs.help: a pause after each gesture, so a person can watch; checks and deadlines are unchanged

outputs.name: steps.json
outputs.help: each step as done: index, verb, arguments, what it read, elapsed milliseconds

outputs.name: <as>.json
outputs.help: the rows a rows step kept, with the picture number they were read from

outputs.name: <name>.bmp
outputs.help: a picture step's capture (<name>.cells.txt in a terminal medium)

requires: a Workshop guest granting input and capture
zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in this Loom session
no other run on this link holding Workshop's input session
tools.recovery: Read steps.json: the last entry is the last step done, and the failure names the step that could not be. Gestures already sent are not undone. A refused input session means another run on this link holds it; wait for that run or cancel it (its cleanup closes the session).

tools.name: nvim-edit
tools.summary: Edit one file through Workshop's Neovim pane -- create, append, insert after or before an anchor line, replace or delete a range -- save it there, and check the saved file is exactly the planned text.
tools.description: Plans every edit against the file's current text (a local read), then drives Neovim as a maker would: open the file with :e, go to the anchor's line, open a line and type, delete a range, write with :w. Typed text stays literal: after opening, 'paste' is set again and autoindent, smartindent, cindent, indentexpr and expandtab are cleared for that buffer (a buffer's indent script can re-enable autoindent); a new file gets Unix line endings. Text is typed in bounded chunks because Neovim reads its input after Workshop's settle fence, which is also why no single row is trusted: after :e and again after :w the tool types a lone `:`, waits until Neovim sits idle in an empty command line (a prompt never does, and ends the run with nothing more typed), and asks Neovim itself -- in one answer carrying a fresh token -- whether its current buffer is exactly the file, whether it is modified, and a digest of its lines. Nothing is typed into a buffer unless it IS the file, is NOT modified and holds exactly what is on disk: a draft never saved, an unsaved change, a buffer that differs from the disk and a buffer Neovim would not leave are all refused untouched. The run passes only when Neovim says the buffer is saved and holds the planned lines AND the file on disk equals the planned text; otherwise expected.txt and actual.txt are kept. An anchor is text that must occur in exactly one line (a range's last anchor is the first line at or after its first).

inputs.name: link
inputs.help: the admitted Workshop link

inputs.name: path
inputs.help: the file, absolute, without spaces or Ex specials (% # | quotes backslash)

inputs.name: edits
inputs.help: a JSON list, applied in order: {"create": text}, {"rewrite": text} (the whole file), {"append": text}, {"after": anchor, "text": text}, {"before": anchor, "text": text}, {"replace": anchor or [first, last], "text": text}, {"delete": anchor or [first, last]}

inputs.name: chunk
inputs.help: bytes of text per typed moment (at least 200)

inputs.name: pace_ms
inputs.help: a pause after each typed chunk, so a person can watch the text arrive

inputs.name: to_unix
inputs.help: accept a file with CRLF line endings and let Neovim write it back with LF; without it such a file is refused. Every file this tool saves is written with LF

outputs.name: edit.json
outputs.help: path, line spans each edit produced, bytes typed, before/expected/after sha256, the disk's and the plan's digests, Neovim's own answers after :e (opened) and after :w (saved), the pane's last top row, verdict (matches, DIFFERS, NOT SAVED, or on a refusal UNSAVED, NOT OPENED, NOT THE FILE)

outputs.name: expected.txt
outputs.help: only when the saved file differs: the planned text

outputs.name: actual.txt
outputs.help: only when the saved file differs: what Neovim wrote

requires: a Workshop guest granting input and capture
the Editor switched to Neovim and its pane open (docs/workshop/neovim.md)
zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in this Loom session
the file readable on this machine (the comparison is a local observation)
tools.example: loom-session run <dir> workshop/nvim-edit --name add-line --input path=<project>/td.cpp --input edits=[{"after":"// ---- rules","text":"constexpr int kCost = 10;"}]
tools.recovery: Read edit.json and, on a difference, expected.txt against actual.txt. The tool does not undo: Neovim's buffer and the file are as the run left them; use Neovim's undo (u) or edit again. Unsaved work is refused before anything is typed into it -- a never-saved draft included, and the typing an interrupted run left: write it (:w) or discard it (:e!) in Neovim, then run again. A retry plans from the file as it is then, so read it first if the interrupted run may have written. A prompt Neovim shows (a swap file's question) is left for you to answer.

tools.name: builder
tools.summary: Drive the Builder pane as a maker would -- choose a recipe, build it, build what the project waits on, arm load-after-build, load what was built, promote, revert, or add it to the load plan -- and follow what the Builder itself says became of the press, to its own endings.
tools.description: Subscribes, through the link, to the Builder's own publications (zengine.builder's BuildAsked v1 and BuildStatus v4; the guest's row must list both under `observe`) BEFORE any key is pressed. Then presses into the Builder (closing its output reader or recipe list first), chooses the named recipe with c, and presses the act's key: build b, frontier f (build and realize what the project waits on), arm Shift+b (the load-after-build switch), load-built Shift+b (the button a finished build offers), promote Shift+p, revert Shift+r, load-it o plus the role and Return, or look (nothing). Every press is settled, so everything it set in motion synchronously has arrived before it returns, marked with this run's correlation for the press: the ask this run made is the BuildAsked its press caused -- taken as ask number N, or refused in the Builder's words -- never the first status to arrive. Its operation is the one the Builder's statuses name beside that ask's number. Build, frontier, load-built and a load-it that loads now are one ask: its build must END (succeeded, FAILED, NO ARTIFACT, did not start, unknown recipe) and, when it asked for realization, its realization must END for that operation (realized or REFUSED) -- two answers, never merged; running, asked and offered are never an ending. A status about a later ask before this one's ending means another build was taken after it, and the run fails as SUPERSEDED rather than take that build's ending; another ask's unknown-recipe refusal, which the Builder folds into the outcome while a build runs, is set aside. The input session is given back right after the press: from then on the pane may be covered, closed or resized. Arm is confirmed by the pane's switch; promote and revert by the realization owner's sentence folded into a status; load-it by the pane's own sentence about the plan row, or, when the built product is loaded now, by that ask's operation, followed like a build. A pane's refusal ends the run in its own words. When a build does not succeed the Builder's own output reader is paged to its end and kept as output.txt. A wait that ends first, or an observation that ends (revoked, or lost with the link), is UNRESOLVED, naming the ask and the operation as far as they are known.

inputs.name: link
inputs.help: the admitted Workshop link

inputs.name: act
inputs.help: build, frontier, arm, load-built, promote, revert, load-it or look

inputs.name: recipe
inputs.help: the recipe to choose first (its name in the catalog); empty keeps the chosen one

inputs.name: role
inputs.help: load-it: the role the artifact will hold (the office its source speaks as)

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.help: how long to wait for the Builder's answer; running out fails as UNRESOLVED, naming the operation, which the Builder carries on with

inputs.name: expect
inputs.help: succeeded, failed or any: which ENDED build outcome passes (any never accepts a build still running)

inputs.name: realize
inputs.help: realized, refused or any: which ENDED realization outcome passes; realized also needs the operation to have asked for one. A load-it row that is resolved counts as realized; pending does not, nor loading -- a load conversation whose end the Builder does not paint, confirmed at the loaded weave's own pane

inputs.name: op
inputs.help: look: the operation to wait for (its build and, when it asked, its realization), pressing nothing -- the way back to an UNRESOLVED run's operation

outputs.name: builder.json
outputs.help: the snapshot before; every word the Builder said after the subscription began, in order, each with its number, its cause and Workshop's history numbers; the ask (its number, taken or refused, the press's correlation) and the operation named beside it; the build ({op, outcome}) and the realization ({asked, op, outcome, detail}) as two entries; seconds from the subscription to the press, the ask, the operation, the build's end and the realization's; any confirmation; unresolved or superseded (stage, op, ask -- null while never known) when the wait did not conclude; the subscription's own account

outputs.name: output.txt
outputs.help: only when a build did not succeed: every line the Builder's output reader showed

requires: a Workshop guest granting input and capture
a guest row that may observe zengine.builder's BuildAsked v1 and BuildStatus v4
the Builder pane open where Workshop describes it
zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in this Loom session
tools.example: loom-session run <dir> workshop/builder --name build-game --input recipe=tower-defense --input act=frontier --input realize=realized --wait 320
tools.recovery: Read builder.json and output.txt. An UNRESOLVED run names its operation once one is numbered, and that operation keeps running in the Builder: run act=look op=<N> to wait for it again -- it presses nothing, so nothing is built twice. A SUPERSEDED run's own ending was never seen because another build was taken after it: its operation's words are in the Builder's output reader (l, then the older build's output); look cannot wait for an operation that is no longer the Builder's latest. Promote and revert change which image runs next and now respectively; neither touches source. A load refused for a changed shape leaves the running weave as it was. A refused subscription means the guest's row does not list the Builder's shapes under `observe` in Workshop's guests file: the maker adds them; nothing was pressed.

tools.name: observe
tools.summary: Follow what one office of a running Workshop publishes, for a while, and keep every word: what an owner says, numbered, with every loss said.
tools.description: Subscribes through the link to one office's publications of the named shapes (the guest's row must list them under `observe`; Workshop's relay refuses anything else in its own words), takes what it is told until `seconds` pass, `count` observations arrived or the subscription ends, then releases it. Every item is kept in order in observed.json: each observation with its number, its decoded fields (decoded with the descriptors the relay sent, so this host need not know the shape), the producer and its incarnation, its cause (this run's own correlation, or 0: this tool presses nothing, so always 0) and the far host's history numbers; each Gap with how many were lost and why; the ending. It holds no input session, so it may run beside a run that does. `read_pause_ms` makes it a deliberately slow reader and `window` a small one, which is how the relay's bounds are seen: occurrences past the window are dropped, counted and said as a Gap, and a `latest` shape keeps only its newest (`coalesced`). The summary counts observations, gaps and what they lost -- a loss is never hidden.

inputs.name: link
inputs.help: the admitted Workshop link

inputs.name: producer
inputs.help: the office whose publications to follow, e.g. zengine.builder or td.game

inputs.name: shapes
inputs.help: Name@version, comma-separated, e.g. BuildAsked@1,BuildStatus@4

inputs.name: latest
inputs.help: comma-separated names of shapes that are whole state: while the window is shut only the newest of each is kept

inputs.name: seconds
inputs.help: how long to follow; running out ends the run, not the producer

inputs.name: count
inputs.help: stop after this many observations (0: no count)

inputs.name: window
inputs.help: words the relay may say unacknowledged (0: its default, 256)

inputs.name: read_pause_ms
inputs.help: a pause after each word taken: a deliberately slow reader

outputs.name: observed.json
outputs.help: every item in order (observations, gaps, the ending) with the subscription's own account: words said, lost (the relay's and this client's), repeated, acknowledged

requires: a Workshop guest whose row may observe the named office's shapes
zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in this Loom session
tools.example: loom-session run <dir> workshop/observe --name builder-words --input producer=zengine.builder --input shapes=BuildAsked@1,BuildStatus@4 --input latest=BuildStatus --input seconds=60 --wait 90
tools.recovery: A refusal in Workshop's words means the guest's row does not list that office and shape under `observe`, or no participant there declares the shape (the application is not loaded): the maker's guests file decides the first. An ending `lost` means the link's session ended: what was said after the last word kept is unknown. Gaps are losses the relay or this client counted: a slower reader or a smaller window loses more.

tools.name: inventory-organize
tools.summary: Name stored Inventory entries and file them in a named folder through the Inventory owner's own operations, without an input session.
tools.description: Lists the collection (InventoryList v2), finds each rule's entry by its label (and schema, when given) plus `contains`: text that must occur in the entry's stored bytes, such as a command's field value -- a byte search, not a decoder. Every rule must match exactly one entry, or nothing is changed. Creates the folder under Root when no Root folder has that name, renames each entry at its listed revision and files it there, then lists again and passes only if every entry reads its new label in that folder. Nothing is executed and no authority is granted.

inputs.help: the admitted Workshop link

inputs.name: plan

outputs.help: each entry's label, schema, folder and revision after the changes

zengine-guest-vocabulary booted in this Loom session

tools.recovery: A view already created stays; move its entries back to main Inventory or leave it (a toolbox restore offers views again). A conflicting active key is refused by the pane and earlier mappings remain.

tools.name: lane
tools.summary: Build targets in a configured Zengine build tree, run one doctest binary's cases by name, or run the official lane (tests/verify.cmake), keeping each command's output and its own exit code.
tools.description: Scoped local work from the external host: CMake and the tree's own test binaries only, as this session's user. op=build runs cmake --build for the named targets; op=case runs <tree>/tests/<binary> with --test-case; op=verify runs cmake -DZEN_BUILD_DIR=<tree> -P <source>/tests/verify.cmake from the checkout, which is the repository's official lane. Each command's whole output is kept as an artifact and its exit code recorded directly. expect=red passes only when the last command fails -- the record a mutation leaves. It configures nothing and edits no source.

inputs.name: tree
inputs.help: an absolute, configured build tree (it holds CMakeCache.txt)

inputs.name: op
inputs.help: build, case or verify

inputs.name: targets
inputs.help: build: comma-separated target names

inputs.name: binary
inputs.help: case: the test binary's name under <tree>/tests, without .exe

inputs.name: cases
inputs.help: case: doctest's --test-case filter (a name, wildcards allowed)

inputs.name: source
inputs.help: verify: the Zengine checkout the tree was configured from

inputs.name: path_prefix
inputs.help: a directory put first on PATH, e.g. a MinGW bin the binaries need

inputs.name: parallel
inputs.help: build: cmake --parallel

inputs.name: expect
inputs.help: pass, or red for a mutation's expected failure

outputs.name: lane.json
outputs.help: each command's argv, exit code, seconds, output size and last lines

outputs.name: <op>-<n>.log
outputs.help: each command's whole output

requires: a configured Zengine build tree and CMake on this machine
the toolchain's runtime directory on PATH (path_prefix) when the binaries need it
tools.example: loom-session run <dir> workshop/lane --name panes-case --input tree=<build tree> --input op=case --input binary=zengine-workshop-panes-tests --input cases="the realize row*"
tools.recovery: Read lane.json and the logs. Nothing is undone: a build writes its tree as any build does. A verify run that was cancelled leaves its tree as far as it got; run it again.

tools.name: repo
tools.summary: Git and a GitHub pull request for one named repository: status, diff, log, show and fetch; stage named paths; commit as a named author with no trailer; push the current branch; open, edit or read a pull request and its checks.
tools.description: Scoped local work from the external host: git in root, and gh for a pull request, as this session's user with that user's own credentials. commit takes author as `Name <email>`, who is also the committer; a message carrying a trailer is refused before anything is written, the made commit is read back (its trailers must be empty, its author and committer the named one) and a repository that carries tests/check_commit_attribution.cmake must pass it. push pushes the current branch to the same name on the remote and refuses the default branch. pr-checks answers what `gh pr checks` says, pending and failing included; run-view reads one workflow run, with --log-failed when asked. It never merges, never enables auto-merge, never force-pushes, never rewrites history and never deletes a branch, a file or a pull request.

inputs.name: root
inputs.help: an absolute path to the Git checkout

inputs.name: op
inputs.help: status, diff, log, show, fetch, add, commit, push, pr-create, pr-edit, pr-view, pr-checks or run-view

inputs.name: paths
inputs.help: add: a JSON list of paths, relative to root

inputs.name: message
inputs.help: commit: the whole message; a trailer in it is refused

inputs.name: author
inputs.help: commit: `Name <email>`, the author and the committer

inputs.name: range
inputs.help: diff, log, show: revisions or a range, e.g. origin/main..HEAD

inputs.name: count
inputs.help: log: how many commits

inputs.name: remote
inputs.help: fetch, push: the remote

inputs.name: branch
inputs.help: push: the branch the checkout must be on (a guard); empty takes the current one

inputs.name: title
inputs.help: pr-create: the pull request's title

inputs.name: body
inputs.help: pr-create, pr-edit: the pull request's description, Markdown

inputs.name: base
inputs.help: pr-create: the base branch; empty is the remote's default

inputs.name: pr
inputs.help: pr-edit, pr-view, pr-checks: the pull request's number

inputs.name: run
inputs.help: run-view: the workflow run's id

inputs.name: log_failed
inputs.help: run-view: the failed steps' logs too

outputs.name: repo.json
outputs.help: each command's argv, exit code, seconds, output size and last lines

outputs.name: <op>-<n>.log
outputs.help: each command's whole output

requires: git on this machine, and gh signed in for the pull-request operations
tools.example: loom-session run <dir> workshop/repo --name commit-story --input root=<checkout> --input op=commit --input author="A Maker <maker@example.org>" --input message="Add the tower defense example"
tools.recovery: Read repo.json and the logs. A refused commit wrote nothing; a made commit that failed its read-back stays made and is named in the failure -- inspect it with op=show before anything is pushed. Nothing is ever pushed by force.
